# How to Use This Book {.unnumbered}

## Reading paths

- **First pass.** Read Volume 1, then Parts III and IV. Everything later depends on them.
- **Deep learning to LLMs.** After Volume 1, go to Part VII (DL foundations), IX (NLP), XI (RL), XII (LLMs) and XIII (agents). Add VIII (vision) and X (generative) as needed.
- **Probabilistic ML.** Parts II.3–II.6, then V and VI, then X.
- **Interview sprint.** Read each chapter's *Summary* and *Interview questions*, then Part XVI. Go back to the derivations whenever an answer starts to feel memorised.

## How each chapter is built

| Block | What to do with it |
|---|---|
| **Sources** box | The free books this chapter draws on. Read them alongside for a second explanation. |
| Derivations | Re-derive them on paper. Cover the text and try to reproduce each step. |
| Code cells | Run them, change them, break them. Every from-scratch version ends with an `assert` against a library. |
| Worked examples | Do the arithmetic yourself before reading the solution. |
| Exercises [E]/[M]/[H] | Easy, medium, hard. Solutions are collapsed, so try first. |
| Interview questions | Answer out loud in under 2 minutes, then compare with the model answer. |

## Notation

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $x, \alpha$ | scalars (italic) |
| $\mathbf{x}$ | column vector (bold lowercase) |
| $\mathbf{A}$ | matrix (bold uppercase) |
| $\mathbf{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$ | data matrix, one example per **row** |
| $\mathbf{w}, \boldsymbol\theta$ | parameters |
| $\mathbf{A}^\top$ | transpose |
| $\|\mathbf{x}\|_2$ | Euclidean norm |
| $\mathbb{E}[X]$, $\operatorname{Var}[X]$ | expectation, variance |
| $p(\mathbf{x})$ | density or mass function |
| $\nabla_{\mathbf{w}} f$ | gradient (same shape as $\mathbf{w}$) |
| $\log$ | natural logarithm unless stated otherwise |

## The free books behind this one

These are the main companions (PDFs in `sources/pdf/`):

- **MML**: Deisenroth, Faisal, Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning*
- **ISLP / ESL**: James et al., *An Introduction to Statistical Learning*; Hastie et al., *The Elements of Statistical Learning*
- **PML1/PML2**: Murphy, *Probabilistic Machine Learning*
- **UDL**: Prince, *Understanding Deep Learning*
- **D2L**: Zhang et al., *Dive into Deep Learning*
- **RLbook**: Sutton & Barto, *Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction*
- **SLP3**: Jurafsky & Martin, *Speech and Language Processing*
- **PRML**: Bishop, *Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning*
- **Boyd**: Boyd & Vandenberghe, *Convex Optimization*
- **ITILA**: MacKay, *Information Theory, Inference, and Learning Algorithms*
- **CS249r**: *Machine Learning Systems*
